paper_name: Operations Management and Strategic Management (Operations Management)
author: Rahul kp
title: Job vs Mass
simple_words: Job production makes one special item per order. Mass production makes the same item again and again in large numbers.

definitions.meaning: Making one or few units as per the ==customer's specific order==, each unit different. Example: ship building, a tailor-made suit.
Continuous making of ==standardised products in large volume== on a fixed line, usually for stock. Example: biscuits, bulbs.
definitions.note: Made for the market, not one customer

key_points: Job = high variety, low volume. Mass = low variety, high volume.
Job uses general-purpose machines; mass uses ==special-purpose machines==.
Job needs skilled labour; mass can run on semi-skilled labour.
!!Batch production lies in between!!: a group of identical units at a time.

insight.text: As variety of products rises, volume falls and cost per unit rises; mass production reverses this.

memory_trick.explanation: Tailor: one customer, own measurements, skilled hands, costly (job). Readymade factory: same shirt in thousands, machines, cheap (mass).

steps: Read: is it to customer order?
exam_tip: In MCQs, words like 'specific order', 'one-off', 'ship', 'bridge' point to job; 'continuous', 'standard', 'assembly line' point to mass.

doubt.question: Is batch production the same as job production?
doubt.answer: No. Batch makes a group of identical units at a time, then switches. Job makes each order as a separate, unique unit.

mistakes.wrong: Mass production uses a process layout
mistakes.right: Mass production uses a ==product (line) layout==; job production uses a process layout.

mistakes.wrong: Job production has the lowest cost per unit
mistakes.right: Job has !!higher cost per unit!!; mass spreads cost over large volume.

mistakes.wrong: Mass production needs highly skilled labour
mistakes.right: Mass production runs on special machines, so semi-skilled labour is enough.

reviewer_note: No past-paper list was given, so past_papers is empty. Cost per unit and skill-level are general tendencies, not fixed rules.

Checker 1: Table row 2 (Layout, Job column) and mistake 1 'right' say job production uses a process (functional) layout. But the note's own examples, ship building in definition 1 and 'ship' and 'bridge' in the exam tip, use a fixed-position layout. In fixed-position layout the product stays in one place and men, machines and materials are brought to it. Correct version: 'Process (functional) layout, or fixed-position layout for large or immovable jobs such as ships and bridges.' Mistake 1 'right' should read: 'Mass production uses a product (line) layout; job production uses a process layout, or a fixed-position layout for very large jobs.'
